_how_to: Corrections the parser cannot work out, keyed by edition id (YYYY-MM-DD). Top-level keys replace edition fields; 'stories' replaces fields of a story by its number.

2026-10-20.summary: Oil is above US$110 and the IEA says it won't settle down soon. China grew on exports, NAB is cutting jobs, and the RBA could raise rates again on Melbourne Cup Day.

02.q: Using an AD/AS diagram, explain how a rise in global oil prices affects inflation and economic growth in an oil-importing economy such as Australia. (6 marks)

03.q: Outline two reasons other than protecting local industry that a government might impose tariffs. Use this story as an example. (4 marks)

04.q: Explain how a fall in iron ore prices affects Australia's terms of trade and current account balance. (4 marks)

05.q: Using a diagram, explain the effects of a US tariff on Australian lamb exporters, US producers and US consumers. (6 marks)

06.q: Discuss the costs and benefits of foreign ownership of essential-service companies in Australia. (6 marks)

07.q: Using the NAB job cuts and the September Labour Force data, distinguish between structural and cyclical unemployment. (4 marks)

08.q: Explain how rising inflationary expectations can make inflation harder to bring down. (4 marks)

09.q: Evaluate how effective monetary policy can be in reducing inflation that is caused by rising global oil prices. (8 marks)
